name: Elapsed-time duration bars
reader_question: How long did each item take to get from one dated stage to the next?
relationship: Elapsed days between the same two dated stages for each item, as zero-based bars sorted by duration.
use_when: Every item has the same two dated stages, such as announcement and effective date
The lag between stages matters more than the calendar position
avoid_when: Calendar position and overlap matter — use swimlane
Items have different stage pairs — the bars would not share a basis; use a table

data_contract.notes: The two stages every item is measured between
from ≤ to; both dates are printed under the item name

units: Calendar days between the two stages; months shown as days ÷ 30.4375 for reading only.

editable: Bars, baseline, gridline and labels as native shapes and text boxes
not_data_bound: Bar lengths are computed from the fixture at build time; editing a date does not resize its bar

table_alternative: A table of item, from date, to date and elapsed days.
variations: Two stacked segments per bar for three dated stages
Sorted by calendar order instead of duration
limitations: Elapsed time does not show which stage was delayed, or whether a delay was intended
Bars share one zero-based axis only if every item measures the same pair of stages

excluded_alternatives.reason: Offset starts make lengths harder to compare and add calendar position that the question does not ask for
